recentItems.title: Famed fashion and costume designer Bob Mackie dies at 87
recentItems.description:
Famed costume designer Bob Mackie died Monday. He was 87 years old.

Mackie was known as the “Sultan of Sequins” for the show-stopping looks he created for famous performers, and his dazzling designs became as memorable as the stars who wore them — think Cher's feathered mohawk headdress at the 1986 Oscars. He designed an estimated 17,000 costumes for Carol Burnett's variety show, including a famous dress made out of a pair of curtains from her 1976 "Gone with the Wind" parody.

Mackie won nine Emmy Awards and a Tony Award and continued dressing stars into the 21st century like Miley Cyrus and Pink.

recentItems.title: Apple TV's 'Widow's Bay' wins big with 14 Emmy Awards
recentItems.description:
There was a big winner during last night’s Emmy Awards for the best in television: The horror comedy "Widow’s Bay" picked up 14 trophies.

Matthew Rhys was crowned best lead actor in a comedy for his role as the mayor of Widow’s Bay, a haunted New England island. His costars Kate O’Flynn and Stephen Root both won supporting actor awards. Rhys also made history by winning two lead actor Emmys at the same ceremony — the Welsh actor also won for his role in the series "The Beast in Me."

Jean Smart also picked up her fifth Emmy Award in a row for best comedy actress in the show "Hacks." The best male dramatic actor was Noah Wyle for his star role in the show "The Pitt." The best variety show winner was the "Late Show with Stephen Colbert," which was canceled by CBS earlier this year.

recentItems.title: Mitch McConnell returns to the Senate after 3-months-long abscence
recentItems.description:
Republican Sen. Mitch McConnell, of Kentucky, was back on Capitol Hill yesterday for the first time since he was hospitalized in June after a fall.

The 84-year-old returned to the Senate floor in a wheelchair with staff by his side. McConnell cast a vote that was needed to move a judicial nomination forward along a Republican party line vote. The former senate majority leader said in a statement he is not yet 100%, but plans to continue physical therapy and return when his conference needs him for the "tough votes." He also said his recovery has been a long and frustrating process and the lingering effects of childhood polio have not made it any easier.

McConnell has the remainder of this year left to finish his final term in Congress.

recentItems.title: Macklemore dropped from Ed Sheeran's tour for saying 'Free Palestine'
recentItems.description:
Macklemore has been dropped from Ed Sheeran’s U.S. tour over comments supportive of Palestinians.⁠
⁠
Macklemore already opened for several shows of Sheeran’s stadium tour. While onstage, the rapper made comments in support of people in Gaza and the West Bank and used the phrase “Free Palestine.” He's been dropped from the remainder of the tour. Sheeran’s promoter, Messina Touring, told "Rolling Stone" that several U.S. venues refused to host concerts with Macklemore on the bill.⁠
⁠
In a statement posted on his Instagram, Macklemore claims that Gillette Stadium owner Robert Kraft called Sheeran and told him Macklemore would not be allowed at his venue. Kraft allegedly also rallied other venue owners against the performer over his political statements. In his social media post, Macklemore writes that he's not a victim while doubling down on his support for Palestinians.⁠
⁠

⁠
Host: Korva Coleman/NPR⁠
Reporter: Isabella Gomez Sarmiento/NPR⁠
Producer: Zayrha Rodriguez/NPR

recentItems.title: Celine Dion returns to the stage after battling rare illness
recentItems.description:
Celine Dion kicked off her 16-show residency in Paris at the Plenitude Arena on Saturday. Wearing a black dress, the Grammy Award-winning singer opened the concert with the French song "On Ne Change Pas," which means "we don’t change" in English. Emotional and with tears in her eyes, Dion thanked the audience throughout the night.⁠
⁠
It was her first performance nearly four years after announcing she had been battling Stiff Person Syndrome, a rare neurological condition that causes stiff limbs and severe muscle spasms.⁠
⁠

recentItems.title: Trump downplays calls for slowdown in AI development
recentItems.description:
President Trump is downplaying concerns about the dangers of artificial intelligence. Anthropic's CEO suggested over the weekend the industry slow its development of AI to ensure more safeguards are put in place. Trump says he doesn’t want to give China any advantage.⁠
⁠
Trump says some of what's being said is exaggerated: "I’m not downplaying, but it’s going to be more good than bad, but a a lot. I’ve said it from the beginning ... whoever wins AI win."

Meanwhile, it’s not clear what kind of slowdown AI company leaders might agree on.⁠
⁠
Anthropic, Google and Microsoft are among NPR's financial supporters.⁠
⁠

recentItems.title: Study: Very hot drinks could triple risk of esophageal cancer
recentItems.description:
According to a large new study, drinking beverages at very hot temperatures on a regular basis could raise the risk of developing cancer of the esophagus.⁠
⁠
The study followed nearly a million tea and coffee drinkers across the U.K. over 14 years. Researchers found that those who regularly drank very hot beverages had three times the risk of developing esophageal cancer compared to those who sipped their drinks warm. The findings are in line with prior studies in Asia, South America and the Middle East.⁠
⁠
The International Agency for Research on Cancer classifies drinks hotter than149 degrees Fahrenheit as probably carcinogenic to humans. Drinking very hot liquids can damage the cells lining the esophagus, and repeated injuries can raise the risk of cancer over time. Experts say it’s best to let hot drinks cool for a few minutes before taking a sip.⁠
⁠

Reporter: Maria Godoy/NPR⁠

recentItems.title: Trump administration resumes work on barrier to stop invasive carp after call from Whitmer
recentItems.description:
The Trump administration says it is restarting work on a barrier to keep invasive carp from reaching the Great Lakes after abruptly halting the construction a few months ago.

The invasive carp can grow several feet long and eat their way through ecosystems, devastating tourism and boating industries. The fish have edged ever closer to Lake Michigan, and after some delays, President Trump sent federal funding to help create a barrier at a choke point in Illinois. But Trump issued an unexplained work-stoppage order in late July.

The barrier work is reportedly resuming after a call to Trump from Michigan Gov. Gretchen Whitmer, a Democrat who was also a critic of the president during the pandemic, but has since had a more cordial relationship.

recentItems.title: U.S. marks 25th anniversary of the 9/11 terrorist attacks
recentItems.description:
A moment of silence was held at 8:46 at ground zero this morning in New York City as the nation observes 25 years since the Sept. 11 terrorist attacks. The moment marked the time the first hijacked plane struck the north tower of the World Trade Center.⁠
Family members gathered and read aloud the names of their loved ones who were killed in New York and at the Pentagon, where 184 people died when American Airlines Flight 77 crashed into the building. The 40 passengers and crew members aboard United Airlines Flight 93 were being remembered in western Pennsylvania, too. Their plane crashed into a field near Shanksville, Pa., after hijackers seized the cockpit. Investigators determined the flight had been headed toward the nation’s capital.⁠
⁠
